newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline stable, still seeking better demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline stable, still seeking better demand.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were little changed on Tuesday. Traders said NYMEX unleaded futures had offered little fresh direction and demand in NWE was fairly relaxed.
They said that U.S. arbitrage was limited though larger cargoes were being booked for the trip. Shipping sources reported a 60,000 tonne cargo booked by Total to go trans-Atlantic in May.

However, they said there was a continued lack of buying interest from players generally, despite depleted U.S. gasoline stocks which were nearly 10 million barrels below year-ago levels according to last week's API report.
U.S. traders estimated gasoline inventories for the week ended May 2 rose 1.5 million barrels.
No outright cargo deals were heard done but Eurograde cargoes were notionally valued around $200 cif for premium unleaded.
Eurograde barges traded and valued around $194 a tonne fob Rotterdam refinery for May 1-15 liftings and regular barges traded at $184 a tonne fob ARA.

However, despite the stable spot markets traders said forward sentiment indicators swaps were looking slightly softer reflecting the limited U.S. demand and possible increased in supply due to fairly healthy refining margins.

Dealers were unconvinced that prices will hold current levels amid evidence that U.S. demand is running only very slightly above last year's levels. They said rich NWE margins may also prompt NWE refiners into boosting output.
May swaps were talked around $1 lower at $192.75/$193.75 fob ARA.
